Complete-case analysis

Aka listwise deletion.

Perform the analysis on the observations for which there is no missing value in the variables involved in the analysis.

In MAR data, missingness in X depends on Y.

Conclusions

MCAR

  • Unbiased estimates of means, variances and regression parameters.
  • Correct standard errors and significance levels (but often larger than if the whole sample was available) \(\Rightarrow\) inefficiencies: lower power, wider CI.

MAR

  • Can yield biased estimates of means, regression parameters and correlations.

  • In regression: in some specific cases, the best solution!

    • Regression with missing values only in the response variable: listwise deletion and multiple imputation are equivalent. If additional predictors available for multiple imputation: multiple imputation should be preferred over listwise deletion.

    • If missing values in the dependent and/or the independent variable that do not depend on the dependent variable: no bias in regression coefficients.

Conclusions

MCAR

  • Downward bias in the estimated variance.
  • Bias in almost any estimate other than the mean.
  • Disturbs the relations between variables.

MAR

  • Downward bias in the estimated variance.
  • Bias in any estimate.
  • Disturbs the relations between variables.

Conclusions

MCAR

  • Unbiased estimates of the means
  • Unbiased estimates of the regression coefficients of the imputation model if the explanatory variables are complete.
  • Downward bias in variance estimates
  • Upward bias in correlation estimates

MAR

  • Unbiased estimates of the means
  • Unbiased estimates of regression coefficients if the variables related to missingness are included in the regression model
  • Downward bias in variance estimates
  • Upward bias in correlation estimates**

Conclusions

MCAR

  • Unbiased means
  • Unbiased regression coefficients and correlations
  • Can yield values that are out of the range of the possible values.
  • Does not take potential heteroskedasticity into account.

MAR

  • Unbiased means
  • Unbiased regression coefficients and correlations
  • Can yield values that are out of the range of the possible values.
  • Does not take potential heteroskedasticity into account.
